q: The arrangement of electrons in an atom was suggested in 1913 by ____.
e: The arrangement of electrons in an atom was suggested in 1913 by Niels Bohr. Niels Bohr is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Electrons move round the nucleus in definite shells or ____.
e: Electrons move round the nucleus in definite shells or orbits. Orbits is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Each shell is numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on, going outwards from the ____.
e: Each shell is numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on, going outwards from the nucleus. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell.

q: They are also known as K shell, L shell, M shell, N shell, and so on, as shown in Figure 3.3, with the first being the ____ shell.
e: They are also known as K shell, L shell, M shell, N shell, and so on, as shown in Figure 3.3, with the first being the K shell. K is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In general, the closer the shell is to the nucleus, the lower is its ____.
e: In general, the closer the shell is to the nucleus, the lower is its energy. Energy is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Each main shell is again divided into a number of sub-shells or ____.
e: Each main shell is again divided into a number of sub-shells or orbitals. Orbitals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The letters used for sub-shells notations: s stands for sharp; p for ____; d for diffuse and f for fundamental.
e: The letters used for sub-shells notations: s stands for sharp; p for principal; d for diffuse and f for fundamental. Principal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The maximum number of electrons in s, p, d and f sub-shells is ____, 6, 10 and 14, respectively.
e: The maximum number of electrons in s, p, d and f sub-shells is 2, 6, 10 and 14, respectively. 2 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The shell number 1 (K shell), has only ____ sub-shell.
e: The shell number 1 (K shell), has only s sub-shell. S is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The shell number 2 (L shell) has s and ____ sub-shells.
e: The shell number 2 (L shell) has s and p sub-shells. P is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The shell number 3 (M shell) has s, p and ____ sub-shells.
e: The shell number 3 (M shell) has s, p and d sub-shells. D is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The shell number 4 (N shell) has s, p, d and ____ sub-shells.
e: The shell number 4 (N shell) has s, p, d and f sub-shells. F is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The electrons always go into the shell nearest to the nucleus which has ____ energy.
e: The electrons always go into the shell nearest to the nucleus which has lowest energy. Lowest is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The shell which is furthest from the nucleus is called the ____ shell.
e: The shell which is furthest from the nucleus is called the valence shell. Valence tells how many electrons an atom typically uses in bonding.

q: The electrons in this shell are known as outer electrons or ____ electrons.
e: The electrons in this shell are known as outer electrons or valence electrons. Valence tells how many electrons an atom typically uses in bonding.

q: These electrons are involved in ____ reactions.
e: These electrons are involved in chemical reactions. Chemical is the idea that completes this fact.

e: The number of outermost shell electron l e le 4, Valence = number of outermost shell electrons. Outermost is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The number of outermost shell electron > 4, Valence = 8 - number of ____ shell electrons.
e: The number of outermost shell electron > 4, Valence = 8 - number of outermost shell electrons. Outermost is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The distribution of electrons in an atom of an element is called the ____ structure.
e: The distribution of electrons in an atom of an element is called the electronic structure. Electronic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The arrangement of all the electrons of an atom of the element in appropriate sub-shells is known as the ____ electronic structure.
e: The arrangement of all the electrons of an atom of the element in appropriate sub-shells is known as the complete electronic structure. Complete is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The representation of the arrangement of valence electrons of an atom of the element in appropriate sub-shells is called the ____ electronic structure.
e: The representation of the arrangement of valence electrons of an atom of the element in appropriate sub-shells is called the essential electronic structure. Essential is the idea that completes this fact.
